intro: Each county and city in Virginia has its own general registrar and electoral board that run voting there. The Virginia Department of Elections oversees them.

elections.name: General election
elections.what: Federal, state, county, and local offices, plus any measures. Your exact ballot depends on where you live.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Any registered voter can vote early in person. Early voting ends at 5 pm on Oct. 31. Your local registrar sets the sites and hours.

src.label: Virginia Department of Elections: upcoming elections

dates.label: Last day to register to vote
dates.detail: This is the last day to register or update your registration the regular way. After that, you can still register in person during early voting or at your polling place on Election Day. You will vote a provisional ballot.

src.label: Virginia Department of Elections: upcoming elections

dates.label: Mail ballot request deadline
dates.detail: Your local registrar must receive your request by 5 pm.

src.label: Virginia Department of Elections: upcoming elections

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 6 am to 7 pm. If you are in line by 7 pm, you can vote. Mailed ballots must be postmarked by Election Day and reach your registrar by noon on Nov. 6. You can also bring your ballot to a drop-off location or your registrar's office by 7 pm on Election Day.

Virginia Department of Elections: absentee voting

id_rule.text: Show an acceptable ID, such as a Virginia driver's license (even if expired), a U.S. passport, or a student ID from a Virginia school. If you don't have one, you can sign an ID Confirmation Statement and vote a regular ballot. If you don't sign it, you vote a provisional ballot.
